meta.title: Iranian Elections
sources: Wikipedia: Iranian and Persian presidential and legislative election articles 1906-2024
Ministry of the Interior figures as reported there

presEras.label: The first republic
presEras.blurb: Four presidential elections in six years, because the first two presidents did not survive their terms: Abolhassan Banisadr was impeached and fled the country in 1981, and Mohammad-Ali Rajai was killed by a bomb two months after replacing him. The war with Iraq ran through all of it.

presEras.label: Reconstruction and reform
presEras.blurb: Rafsanjani rebuilt the economy after the war and Mohammad Khatami won in 1997 with 69% on a reformist platform and a turnout of 80%, the largest mandate the office has recorded. What the presidency could not do with it became the argument of the next twenty years.

presEras.label: The Ahmadinejad years
presEras.blurb: A conservative outsider won the 2005 runoff and was returned in 2009 in the most disputed election in the republic's history, which produced the largest street protests since 1979. Hassan Rouhani's win in 2013 turned on the negotiations that became the nuclear deal.

presEras.label: Disqualification and abstention
presEras.blurb: Turnout has fallen at every presidential election since 2017 as the Guardian Council has narrowed the field further each time. Ebrahim Raisi was elected in 2021 on the lowest turnout in four decades, died in a helicopter crash in May 2024, and the snap election that followed drew under 40% in its first round.

legEras.label: The Constitutional Revolution
legEras.blurb: Persia's first parliament was won in 1906 by a merchant and clerical alliance that forced a constitution out of the Qajar shah. It was bombarded and dissolved two years later, restored, and then squeezed between Russian and British occupation zones until the coup of 1921.

legEras.label: Under the Pahlavis
legEras.blurb: Reza Khan used the army to shape the 1923 elections and the court managed every one that followed. The interlude is 1943 to 1953, when occupation and then Mosaddegh's National Front made the Majlis briefly matter again; the 1953 coup ended it, parties were banned from the 1954 election, and the 1960 result was so openly rigged that the Shah annulled it.

legEras.label: One party
legEras.blurb: In 1975 the Shah abolished the two tame parties he had allowed and declared the Rastakhiz Party the only legal one, telling Iranians who disagreed to leave the country. It won all 268 seats. The revolution was four years away.

legEras.label: The Islamic Republic
legEras.blurb: Twelve elections to the Majlis since the revolution, contested between factions rather than parties and fought on a field the Guardian Council draws before the campaign starts. Reformists won a landslide in 2000 and were largely barred from the ballot by 2004; turnout has fallen from 71% in 1996 to about 41% in 2024, the lowest the republic has recorded.
